name: Peleg Sprague
equipment: Leather jacket, a Navy surplus deck jacket with U.S.N. on the back, over a wool shirt
Flare pistol (a Navy Very pistol off the subchaser he served on, kept for signalling his grandfather's boat), loaded
Wood axe, from the woodpile at the Captain's House
A canvas tool roll, a coil of manila line, a block and tackle, and the know-how to hang a church bell, he hopes
The key to the Union Church tower, which he has had since 16 August and has not given back
A wristwatch with a luminous dial, Navy issue, which he checks against the tide table
features: The Family Name (Old Family origin: received and told things among the old families of a region, with advantage on Persuasion checks with them; once per scenario an introduction or meeting with someone of standing without a check; knows the reputation and scandals of prominent local families; and the old debts and grudges come with the name). He is a Sprague of the Captain's House, the oldest name on Carrow; the island expects him to keep its secrets, and on the big tides the bell knows his name
Held the Line (Veteran: advantage on fear checks while a conscious ally is within 10 ft of him; once per short rest, when Panic would take him at Dread 5, he acts normally instead)
Drill: Close Quarters (Veteran: he doesn't have disadvantage on ranged attacks with a Sidearm or a shotgun against a creature within 5 ft of him; it changes no number on his sheet)
Second Wind (Veteran, 2nd level: once per short rest, as a bonus action, he regains 1d10 + 3 hit points, and loses 1 Dread if he is at Dread 3 or higher)

Service: Sapper (Veteran, 3rd level: he is proficient with dynamite, can set, fuse and disarm charges safely, and his thrown dynamite uses DC 8 + proficiency + DEX; he learned it clearing a wreck at New London, and he can undo anything Galen Coombs sets)

Grease Under the Nails (Mechanic background: he runs the Harbor boat shed and marine railway; boatmen and mechanics talk to him as one of their own, and a few minutes with an engine tells him what is wrong with it without a check, including whether someone made it go wrong)

personality.traits: I grin at trouble. I'd rather fix a thing than talk about it, and I talk about it anyway, all the time, to anyone holding a wrench. I call my great-grandmother 'the Captain' and so does everyone else, behind her back.
personality.ideals: A man ought to be able to say what his family did, good or bad, and stand up straight afterward. I didn't used to think about it. I think about it all the time now.
personality.bonds: Gran'ther Orpha, the Captain, ninety pounds and seventy-three years old and the only person on Carrow I'm afraid of. Mattie Grindle, whom I am going to marry if she ever lets me finish a sentence. The island, all of it, even the parts I don't like.
personality.flaws: I rang the bell on 16 August because the Captain told me to, and it worked, and I've told nobody but Mattie, because the Captain said not to. I have been keeping her secret without knowing what it is, and I am about to find out it is the kind of secret that drowns people. I do not believe the bell can call me. It can.

appearance: A wiry, quick, curly-haired young man of twenty-four with a sunburned grin, grease on his knuckles, the Sprague long jaw and grey eyes, and a Navy tattoo of an anchor on his forearm that his great-grandmother has never been told about. Navy deck jacket, dungarees, rubber boots, a watch with a luminous dial.
backstory: Peleg Sprague is Orpha Sprague's great-grandson, the last Sprague on Carrow under seventy, raised in the Captain's House; his father, Orpha's grandson, was lost at sea off Little Shag in 1919 while Peleg was in the Navy, and his mother went back to her people in Rockland. He joined the Navy at eighteen in 1918 and served as a motor machinist's mate on a wooden subchaser out of New London, hunting U-boats that were never there, and came home in 1919 to fix every engine on the island. He runs the Harbor's boat shed and marine railway at the head of the Bar, and he sleeps there on fine nights. On 15 August, the night after Enoch Farr's funeral, the Captain called him into her room and told him to take the key to the church tower and ring the bell at the bottom of the next night's tide, by hand, for as long as he heard another bell, and not to tell anyone, especially the minister. He did. He heard the other bell, under the sea, stop. In the morning they found Sophronia Coombs standing at the tide line in her nightgown. Then the minister sent the church bell away to be recast, and the Captain would not explain herself to anyone, and two more people walked into the sea.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Peleg is the party's best friend on Carrow and the one whose life is on the line first: if the party do nothing, he is the one called on 14 October, because he sleeps in the boat shed at the head of the Bar, nearer the Point than anyone else of the blood (unless Dr. Thurlow has gone down to the Point to watch, in which case it is the doctor). He is CLUE C2 (he rang and it worked) as soon as the party trust him, and he can hang the recast bell with Kingsley Trask if the party help: three hours with block and tackle. He is a good mechanic, a steady sailor, a good man in a fight with a wood axe and a flare pistol, and brave in a grinning, careless way that should frighten the party once they know the rules. He is the natural choice, in the end, for the hand of the five families' blood that rings the bell for the names, and he will do it if Orpha cannot.
dmNotes.voice: Quick, cheerful Down East with Navy slang on top: 'shipshape', 'scuttlebutt', 'aye aye, Captain' to his great-grandmother. Explains engines to people who did not ask. Goes quiet and serious, suddenly, when he talks about the night of 16 August.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: keep the bell from taking anyone else. Secondary: find out what the Captain knows, and make her say it. Tertiary: marry Mattie Grindle, which he now suspects means making his family say it first.
dmNotes.secrets: When he rang on 16 August he heard, through the drowned bell, a woman's voice saying 'Thank you'. He has not told even Mattie that. Second secret: he knows Galen Coombs has dynamite; he sold Galen the blasting caps from the old quarry stores in September, not knowing what for.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: friendly, curious and helpful from the first day, especially to anyone who can talk engines or boats. Toward Orpha: love, exasperation and fear. Toward Kingsley Trask: friendship and a guilty secret. Toward Mattie: devotion. Toward Galen Coombs: a cousin's wary respect; Galen paid for his Navy tattoo.
